answer:
**Temperature controls how sharply score differences become probabilities.** InfoNCE divides similarities by tau before softmax. A small tau makes a slight similarity advantage dominate, focusing the loss on high-scoring competitors. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.00020) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10084)

For one positive score 0.8 and one negative score 0.7, tau=1 gives positive probability about 0.525; tau=0.1 gives about 0.731. If the negative instead scores 0.9, the low-temperature loss reacts strongly to that mistake.

The derivative with respect to score j is $(p_j-\mathbf1[j=+])/\tau$. This shows both rescaling and concentration. However, if the positive already wins by a fixed margin, wrong-candidate probabilities vanish exponentially as tau approaches zero, and gradients can vanish despite the reciprocal-temperature factor.

**Very low temperature is not free hard-negative mining.** False negatives become especially damaging, numerical stability matters, and ties have different limiting behavior. Use stable log-sum-exp and explicit multiple-positive handling. Tune temperature through retrieval performance and embedding diagnostics rather than assuming sharper probabilities always create better representations.

**Technical details and references.**

For positive score $s_+$ and candidates $s_j$, InfoNCE is $L=-s_+/\tau+\log\sum_j e^{s_j/\tau}$. Its score derivative is $(p_j-\mathbf1[j=+])/\tau$. Lower temperature concentrates probability on high-scoring candidates and magnifies mistakes involving hard negatives. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.00020) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10084)

As $\tau\to0$, log-sum-exp approaches the maximum score after appropriate scaling. If a negative beats the positive, it dominates the gradient; if the positive wins by a fixed margin, the exponential suppression can make gradients vanish despite the $1/\tau$ factor. Ties require separate treatment. Very low temperatures amplify false negatives and numerical sensitivity. Choose temperature using retrieval quality and representation diagnostics, with stable log-sum-exp and an explicit treatment of duplicate positives.
